newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse gets new first-tier listing.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse gets new first-tier listing.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Tuesday the number of first-tier listings would rise to seven this week as one more company joins in trading.
Vehicle parts maker Compa SA, based in Sibiu in Transylvania in central Romania, would start trade on Wednesday, a bourse statement said.
Compa has a share capital of around 74.2 billion lei in shares with a nominal value of 1,000 lei each.

Its main shareholder is the State Ownership Fund, with 50.95 percent. Employees hold 24.53 percent and a stake of 18.99 percent was sold off under a mass privatisation scheme. Other stockholders have the rest.
Compa had a net profit of 11.5 billion lei last year, up from 7.3 billion in 1995.
The company's future plans include boosting turnover by an average annual rate of up to five percent over 1998-2000, when it plans to invest some 50 billion lei in re-equipment.
Brokers welcomed the new listing, saying any addition to the first tier was bound to increase share liquidity and capital inflows from investors.
The Bucharest stock exchange lists 38 companies on its second tier. ($=7,182)
